title: Real textbook problems: pass@k
takeaway: rl is ahead of base at every k in the point estimate (pass@1 62.5% vs 50.0%; pass@32 100.0% vs 100.0%).
note: n=4 textbook theorems; k=1..4096; base and rl. textbook_law: base 62.5%/pass@32 100.0%, rl 12.5%/pass@32 100.0%; control: base 35.9%/pass@32 100.0%, rl 51.6%/pass@32 100.0%.

title: Restricted families: horizon in written lines (theorems unseen in training)
takeaway: on theorems absent from training no family holds up for long: armC on and_tower reaches about 5 written lines, base on and_tower reaches about 4 written lines; rl trails base on and_tower.
note: 1 families; n* at pass@8>=50% over size cells with >=5 unseen items only (theorems in base's pretraining set or the RL pool are excluded; they make up most of the smallest sizes); a short tick at the left edge marks a model that fails at the smallest unseen size; >= marks a censored horizon (never dropped below 50% in the tested range); base, rl, armC. Including training theorems, base reaches n*=2 on and_tower.

title: Glue: does capability compose?
takeaway: compositionality varies by operator: BOX: rl is highest (R=1.455); CHAIN: base is lowest (R=0.427); CASE: R=0 for both models.
note: R = joined pass@1 / product of mastered parts' pass@1, pooled per operator; AND n=1; CHAIN n=1; CASE n=1; BOX n=1; parts' pass@1 from the renamed parts for 0 and the original pool items for 8 (item, model) pairs.

title: Skills: RL pass@1 by length and special skill
takeaway: RL's pass@1 is 50.0% with no special skill needed, 0.0% when a case split is required and 3.1% when the proof is classical.
note: n=60 skill_pool items (direct + legacy-imported runs), rl only; shaded band: 95% item-level bootstrap CI. Same items, pass@1: base vs rl on their 60 common items (no special skill: 31.2% vs 50.0%, case_split: 3.1% vs 0.0%, classical: 6.2% vs 3.1%).

title: Law x substitution size
takeaway: base peaks at s=0 (62.5%), rl peaks at s=0 (87.5%).
note: n=120 instances over 1 schemas (mt), pooled per item at each s; 1 instances seen in training excluded.

title: Free lines: the cost of padding
takeaway: at W=5 written lines, rl solves 75.0% of natural theorems but only 93.8% once those lines are padding.
note: 3 distinct padded items pooled across pad types P1-shared (each unpadded theorem counted once); natural = gen_ctrl at the same W (1 items at W=5), drawn from the dev set the RL hill-climb selected on, so rl's natural curve is optimistic.

title: Prefix completion: finishing someone else's proof
takeaway: with 1 line left rl finishes 100.0% vs base 20.0%; with 3 lines left rl finishes 30.0% vs base 0.0%.
note: items: base=40, rl=40; pooled success rate by lines left (L-j), bins with <20 items omitted; base vs rl.

title: EDL: nats per example to pick up a new pattern
takeaway: rl's EDL is lower on 0/1 classes (0 with no overlap between the two data orders), but rl also starts with lower test loss on 1/1 and EDL tracks the starting loss (Spearman nan); per nat of test loss that training removes, rl costs as much as or more than base on 1/1 classes.
note: 1 classes, base vs rl; EDL* per example at the learning rate with the smallest online code length, including the ln(1) cost of choosing among the learning rates (lr 0 = no update is one of them); 2 data orders. Null control (heldout_cap6, data the models already know): n/a. Runs: edl2-base-8-4, edl2-rl-8-4.

title: Likelihood: how surprised is base by RL's proofs?
takeaway: on rl's crux proofs base assigns about 3.5 nats/line less than rl.
note: median log p per written line of the scored proof, base vs rl, by proof set; runs likelihood-a037da66f05b0016. The last two rows (neutral minimal proofs, rl's own proofs) are the same 0 gen_ctrl theorems rl solves and base never does (p_hat_base=0); the minimal proofs come from the minlen labeller.

title: Steering: base pushed toward rl
takeaway: adding the RL-base direction to base does not move it: the best of 2 (layer, alpha) settings scores 18.8% vs 27.5% unsteered (inside base's 95% CI), but subtracting it from rl costs -8.8 points (47.5% -> 56.2%).
note: pooled pass@1 over interp_eval_dev, interp_eval_sealed, textbook_dev; delta (RL - base mean activation difference at proof positions) is added at proof positions only. interp_eval_dev/sealed dominate the pooled item count (base alone on textbook_dev is 50.0%).

title: Weight interpolation: base -> rl
takeaway: pass@1 rises from 31.2% (alpha=0) to 70.3% (alpha=1) with most of the gain between alpha=0.5 and 1.
note: fixed 150-theorem subset (dev L8-11 + sealed L12-14 gen items), pass@1 and pass@128 on the same items; base=alpha 0, rl=alpha 1. dev L8-11 was the RL hill-climb's selection metric; pass@1 on the sealed set alone: alpha 0 12.5%, alpha 0.5 25.0%, alpha 1 37.5%.

title: Probes: what do the activations add beyond position?
takeaway: next_rule probe accuracy by layer, base vs rl.
note: layers emb, 0, 1, 2, 3; next_rule = the rule of the line about to be written. lines_to_go R2 at the deepest layer: base 0.500, rl 0.500 vs missing from the line index alone; on longer (OOD) proofs it is negative for both (base 0.300, rl 0.300). Majority-class next_rule accuracy: missing.
